title: Regression
summary: Explain what regression predicts (a continuous number) and distinguish it from classification.
objectives: Fit a LinearRegression model on one feature with model.fit(X, y)
Read the slope (coef_) and intercept (intercept_) of the best-fit line
Predict a continuous number for a new, unseen input with model.predict()
Sanity-check a prediction against the possible range of the answer

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

Regression predicts a **number**, such as a price, a temperature or an exam score. That is different from classification, where the answer is a category. Linear regression draws the best-fit straight line through the data: the line that stays as close as possible to every point. In this lab you will load `study_hours.csv` (30 fictional students: hours studied and exam score), fit a `LinearRegression` model and print its slope and intercept, the two numbers that describe the line. You will then predict the score for 7.5 hours of study, a value that is not in the file, and check that the prediction is a sensible mark between 0 and 100. A prediction outside that range would be a warning sign, not a result to trust.

segments.title: Lab: predict an exam score from study hours

lab.title: Predict an exam score from study hours
lab.objective: Fit a LinearRegression on hours_studied versus exam_score, predict the score for 7.5 hours and sanity-check the result.
lab.instructions:
The file study_hours.csv has 30 rows with two columns: hours_studied and exam_score. The starter code already loads it into df.

1. Make X = df[["hours_studied"]] (double brackets: a DataFrame with one column) and y = df["exam_score"].
2. Create model = LinearRegression() and train it with model.fit(X, y).
3. Store slope = model.coef_[0] and intercept = model.intercept_. Print them rounded to 2 decimals:
Slope: <number>
Intercept: <number>
4. Predict for new_hours = 7.5, a value that is not in the file: build new_data = pd.DataFrame({"hours_studied": [new_hours]}) and store predicted_score = model.predict(new_data)[0]. Print it rounded to 1 decimal:
Predicted score for 7.5 hours: <number>
5. Sanity check: an exam score must be between 0 and 100. Store reasonable = 0 <= predicted_score <= 100 and print:
Reasonable: True

Round only when printing, with round(value, 2) and round(value, 1); keep the variables themselves unrounded.
lab.constraints: Use LinearRegression from sklearn.linear_model. Keep the names df, X, y, model, slope, intercept, new_hours, new_data, predicted_score and reasonable. Do not type the slope, intercept or prediction in by hand; they must come from the fitted model. No input().

lab.solution:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

df = pd.read_csv("study_hours.csv")

X = df[["hours_studied"]]
y = df["exam_score"]

model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

slope = model.coef_[0]
intercept = model.intercept_
print("Slope:", round(slope, 2))
print("Intercept:", round(intercept, 2))

new_hours = 7.5
new_data = pd.DataFrame({"hours_studied": [new_hours]})
predicted_score = model.predict(new_data)[0]
print("Predicted score for 7.5 hours:", round(predicted_score, 1))

reasonable = 0 <= predicted_score <= 100
print("Reasonable:", reasonable)
